policy_weighted.description: Policy-heavy feed: 5 policy, 3 general political, 2 partisan messages.

messages.text: I support expanding school voucher programs so parents have more choices about where their children attend school.

comments.author: Jordan Lee
comments.text: Choice is good, but public schools need support too.

comments.author: Maya R.
comments.text: More options would help families who feel stuck.

comments.author: Sam Carter
comments.text: I'd want to know how the program would be funded.

messages.text: Thanks to everyone who came to tonight's town hall. I heard a lot of good questions, and I am taking your concerns back to the campaign team.

comments.author: Riverton Parent
comments.text: Appreciated the chance to ask about local schools.

comments.author: Chris D.
comments.text: Good turnout tonight.

messages.text: I want to protect Medicare and lower prescription drug costs by allowing the federal government to negotiate prices for more medications.

comments.author: Elena
comments.text: Lower drug prices would make a huge difference for my parents.

comments.author: Pat R.
comments.text: What happens to new drug development?

comments.author: Nate W.
comments.text: This is a practical idea if the savings are real.

messages.text: We are getting close to the end of the month. Every small donation helps us keep the campaign on the road and talking with voters across the district.

comments.author: Liam
comments.text: Just chipped in for the first time.

comments.author: Avery
comments.text: Keep going!

messages.text: I support a higher tax rate on very high incomes while keeping taxes lower for middle-income families and small businesses.

comments.author: Dylan
comments.text: Targeting the very top seems fair to me.

comments.author: Grace
comments.text: Would this apply to small business owners too?

comments.author: R. Taylor
comments.text: The details on brackets would matter.

messages.text: I am proud to be a Democrat. Our party believes government can be a force for expanding opportunity and protecting working families.

comments.author: Taylor
comments.text: Glad to see candidates own their party label.

comments.author: Morgan K.
comments.text: Party labels do not tell me enough on their own.

comments.author: Dee
comments.text: Proud Democrat too.

messages.text: I support expanding clean-energy incentives to speed up the transition away from fossil fuels and create more jobs in clean manufacturing.

comments.author: Casey
comments.text: Job creation is the strongest part of this argument.

comments.author: Jordan
comments.text: How quickly could this scale?

comments.author: M. Stone
comments.text: I care most about the cost to households.

messages.text: Election Day is coming up. Make a plan to vote, remind a friend or neighbor, and check the latest information from your local election office.

comments.author: Jules
comments.text: My family is voting early this year.

comments.author: Ben
comments.text: Already made my plan.

messages.text: I support expanding community-based alternatives to incarceration for low-level, nonviolent offenses while focusing prison resources on serious violent crime.

comments.author: Chris
comments.text: Evidence-based reforms make sense to me.

comments.author: Nina
comments.text: I would want strong accountability measures too.

comments.author: Alex J.
comments.text: Public safety has to stay the priority.

messages.text: I have never supported Donald Trump, and I will not be afraid to push back when his agenda conflicts with what I believe is best for our communities.

comments.author: Erin
comments.text: Thank you for saying it plainly.

comments.author: Cole
comments.text: This tells me more about party than policy does.

comments.author: Riley
comments.text: I disagree, but at least the position is clear.
